what_this_is: Apple | halo_rev_a | halo_replica, one row per axis. Five lanes measured Apple's board and nobody had set our own two boards against each other. This file is that comparison, and it is the artifact DECISIONS.md D23 asked for: it converts twenty-two assertions into measured differences, or says CANNOT DETERMINE and names what would settle it.
the_asymmetry_that_governs_every_row: THE THREE OBJECTS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING, and no row means anything until that is stated. Apple's AirTag is a shipped product. halo_rev_a is a routed, DRC-checked, priced KiCad design with 62 footprints, 49 vias and 255 track segments. halo_replica is a MEASURED DRAWING: one face, no copper, no nets, no netlist, no DRC, no price, and no possibility of any of those, because nothing in it was ever a schematic. A Replica row that wins on fidelity has not thereby won anything a person can build.

judging_axes.F: FIDELITY TO APPLE — does this object reproduce what Apple actually built. The Replica's stated purpose (Leif: 'a perfect copy of the internal airtag stuff').
judging_axes.B: BUILDABILITY — can it be ordered, assembled and checked. Measured against published capability pages and against this repo's own DRC/DFM/cost outputs.
judging_axes.G: FITNESS FOR GOAL.md — a cheap open Find My puck, an embeddable circuit block in any outline, and peer-to-peer ranging between Leif's own sensors.

better_is_not_automatic: D23, verbatim: 'some of Core's divergences will survive comparison — the deleted amplifier looks likely.' It did. So did four more. Every row names the axis it is judged on, and where the axes disagree the row says so instead of picking the flattering one. CLOSER TO APPLE IS NOT A SYNONYM FOR BETTER and is never used as one here.
